hypothesis: Question: does the hourly-rental structure transfer to a later period better as an additive (squared_error) or multiplicative (Poisson log-link, or log1p target) relationship within the same HistGradientBoosting learner? Prior evidence: idea-baseline-2 (HGB, all features, squared error) reached development RMSE 59.99 / equal-date MAE 40.95, while idea-ea0e19 dropped elapsed_day/yr and imposed a parametric log-trend, ending at 122.13 — its own forward folds showed the plain log branch was worst in the most recent fold (140.6 vs 116.6 raw), which revised my view: removing the tree's direct access to yr/elapsed_day level information hurt, and a pure log target may shrink peak-hour predictions that dominate RMSE. Contrasting expected outcomes: (A) Poisson loss keeps the multiplicative hour x working-day x weather scaling and matches or beats squared error on forward RMSE (<= ~58 on development) and improves equal-date MAE; (B) squared error remains best on RMSE because RMSE is dominated by peak counts and Poisson under-weights large residuals; (C) log1p target wins on equal-date MAE but loses on RMSE, replicating the ea0e19 pattern. The program selects the branch by mean RMSE over two forward 61-day holdouts using only training dates, reports per-branch fold RMSE and per-date MAE, refits the selected branch on all training rows, and reports any fallback. Only baseline HGB hyperparameters are held fixed, so a single factor (objective/target transform) is varied. Unverified exploratory expectation; one city/two years cannot establish general benefit.
